_why: Ground truth for numeric fidelity, shared by TWO implementations so they cannot drift apart. Generated from automation/phase-b/content_generator.py's check_numeric_fidelity() — the original, whose every rule documents a false positive that once made the enforcer refuse to ship correct content. code/content-fidelity.js is a port and must agree on every case here. Regenerate with scripts/gen-fidelity-fixture.py, never by hand: hand-editing an expectation turns a spec into a rationalisation of whatever the code now does.

cases.name: a genuinely invented number is flagged
generated: Inflation cooled to 2.4%, the lowest in 40 months.

cases.name: a faithful restatement is clean
trailing sentence punctuation is not a new number
insignificant trailing zeros match
thousands separators match
percent is significant: bare 40 does not satisfy 40%
a range written with the unit once
percent spelled out matches the symbol
a number word matches its digit
a digit matches its number word
multiple generated texts are all checked
THE KNOWN LIMIT: a garbled restatement of a real number is NOT caught
cases.source: A 90-day pause prevents tariffs rising to 125%
generated: A 90-day pause on tariffs from 125% to 125%

cases.name: no numbers anywhere is clean
generated: Shipping attacks continued in the region

cases.name: a number in the source but absent from the text is not a suspect
percentage points spelled out
a decimal invented from a whole number is flagged
numbered list markers are structure, not claims
markdown-style numbered markers too
a YEAR at the start of a line is still a claim, not a marker
generated: 2021. was the last time it was this low

cases.name: a number mid-sentence is untouched by the list rule
